cultural.vision_reason: The piece is a head-shawl made from two printed kanga cloths — a textile strongly associated with Swahili coastal dress — even though the accompanying garment terms (dishdasha, sirwal, waqaya) reflect Gulf/Omani-Zanzibari mixed vocabulary; the kanga material itself is a genuine Swahili product.

physical.title: head-cover; head-shawl; kanga
physical.summary: Woman's head-cover or head-shawl (leso or shayla) made from two floral printed red and black cotton kanga cloths sewn together along their widths with an added border of hand-woven metallic thread (zarrie) band with a long green fringe (called hatheeya). This head-shawl can be worn draped over another head-covering (waqaya, 2011,6003.38). The complete outfit includes a contrasting calf-length dress (dishdasha, 2011,6003.36) and baggy trousers (sirwal, 2011,6003.37).

cultural.vision_reason: A purple cotton head-cover with woven border trim and chin-strap, matching a documented Swahili/coastal East African women's dress ensemble (worn with dishdasha and trousers); this style of head-covering is plausible for Swahili dress traditions.

physical.title: head-cover
physical.summary: Woman's head-cover (waqaya or lihaf) made of purple cotton with a border sewn around the edges of orange wool fabric with floral patterns and golden threads. Worn over the head and fastened with a chin-strap made of black wool embellished with plaited metallic trim (seem or talli). Worn over a contrasting dress (dishdasha, 2011,6003.36) and baggy trousers (2011,6003.37). Can also be worn under a second head covering (kanga or leso, and two different head coverings (2011,6003.39).
